page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance within the E2 family. It provides 2 vCPUs derived from a fractional 0.5 physical core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. The CPU topology includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction set extensions like AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage is not included by default, and there are no dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reflect its resource-constrained, shared-core profile. In single-core CPU testing via stress-ng, the instance achieves an average score of 2642.19, whereas multi-core stress-ng performance falls into the weak category at 2642.78. Geekbench scores remain low across categories, with 661.0 for single-core and 682.0 for multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate limited throughput, recording 6.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 4.83 GB/sec for writes. PassMark metrics reflect similar trends, with a CPU score of 3105.59 and a memory score of 817.13. Web serving throughput reaches 0.63 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations hit 0.82 million operations per second.

Designed for budget-conscious, light-duty workloads, the e2-medium leverages shared physical resources to maintain high resource density at an entry-level operational profile. The key architectural tradeoff is the non-dedicated CPU allocation, which causes performance bottlenecks under sustained multi-threaded compute demands or high-memory bandwidth operations. Consequently, this server instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, low-traffic background tasks, basic development environments, or minor utility microservices that do not require continuous full-core CPU performance.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is an entry-level shared-core instance in the E2 family. It is equipped with 2 vCPUs based on half of an Intel Xeon physical core running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 4.0 GB of RAM. It features 16 MB of L3 cache and standard hardware extensions such as AVX, AES, and FMA, while omitting local storage and GPU hardware. Benchmark results highlight an average single-core stress-ng score of 2642.19, but multi-core and memory throughput metrics are limited due to the shared core model, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 682.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 6.36 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost efficiency for low-intensity computing by sharing physical hardware. It is suitable for microservices, lightweight web servers, dev environments, and low-concurrency background processing tasks.
